I didn't run anything here. These probabilities are priors from how ReLU MLPs trained with Adam usually behave, not values computed from the benchmark tables.

**Strongest expected interactions:**
- **28 (learning rate up when it is already high):** this should hurt much more, because training tends to diverge at rates of 0.278 to 1. Effect LOWER.
- **5 (width down when width is already small):** shrinking an already narrow network should cost more accuracy. Effect LOWER.
- **10 and 24 (alpha up when alpha is mid or low):** raising alpha mainly hurts in the high band (0.129 to 1), so the effect is less negative elsewhere. Effect HIGHER.
- **27 (alpha down when alpha is mid):** lowering alpha helps most when alpha is high. Effect LOWER under mid.
- **19 (batch size up when it is already high):** at batch 256 there are very few update steps per epoch on these small datasets. Effect LOWER.
- **13 (batch size down when it is already small):** shrinking a large batch adds many updates, but shrinking a small one adds noise for little gain. Effect LOWER.
- **26 (batch size down at high learning rate):** small batches with a high learning rate make training noisier. Effect LOWER.
- **22 (alpha down at small batch size):** sklearn-style L2 scales by 1/batch_size, so small batches get stronger effective regularization. Effect HIGHER.
- **7 and 11 (width changes at depth 1):** width probably matters more in single-layer networks.
- **4, 12 and 17:** these are weaker effects that depend on the learning rate.

Most other pairs are close to neutral.
